headline: Over 2,300 tourists evacuated from Sajek amid clashes and gunfire
summary: Security forces conducted a joint operation to rescue stranded visitors after a road blockade and gunfight involving the UPDF.
details: More than 2,300 tourists were evacuated from the Sajek road in Rangamati’s Baghaichhari upazila today following clashes between blockade supporters and law enforcers.
The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) stated that the army and police made joint security arrangements to ensure the safe passage of the stranded tourists.

The incident began when blockaders obstructed the road at Gangaram Bazar around 10:00 am, stopping vehicles carrying tourists. Tensions escalated when blockaders allegedly began throwing bricks and stones at law enforcers and tourists.

According to the ISPR, armed members of the United People's Democratic Front (UPDF) fired 30 to 40 rounds at law enforcers and tourists around 11:00 am, prompting the army to return fire in self-defence.
Rangamati Superintendent of Police Muhammad Abdur Rakib confirmed that five army personnel and two police members were injured in the incident, though no tourists were harmed.
The UPDF spokesperson, Angya Marma, denied the reports of a gunfight, claiming instead that security personnel fired shots to break up a peaceful road blockade by local residents.
The blockade, which started at 6:00 am, had left approximately 2,350 people stranded before the situation was brought under control after 1:00 pm.

headline_marked: 1,512 hospitalised as [[dengue claims 4 more lives]] in 24 hours
headline: 1,512 hospitalised as dengue claims 4 more lives in 24 hours
summary: The national death toll has risen to 368, with over 118,000 total cases reported according to the DGHS.
details: At least four people died of dengue and 1,512 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8am today, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the four fatalities, two were reported in Mymensingh division, while one death occurred in each of the Dhaka North and South City Corporations.
The latest figures bring the country's total dengue death toll to 368, with the total number of cases reaching 118,502.
Currently, 6,023 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across the country.
